il_c_north_falls.blurb: North Falls is the main section of the Jackson Falls canyon in Shawnee National Forest, in southern Illinois, running from Royal Arches Wall through to Wizard Wall. Bolted sport climbing dominates, with a solid minority of trad and a few top-rope lines and boulder problems. Grades run from easy fifth class up to 5.13, but most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12. Royal Arches Wall and The Doors hold the most climbs, with Spleef Peak and Wizard Wall next. Jackson Falls has tight-grained sandstone, and the canyon as a whole climbs most comfortably from September through December, with March to May also good but wetter.

nh_yellowjacket_area.blurb: Yellowjacket Area covers the western slope of Bald Knob in Waterville Valley, New Hampshire, where a great number of boulders and small cliffs are scattered down the hillside, reaching as much as half a mile below the top. Bouldering is the main draw, from one-move lowballs to tall highballs, mostly V0 to V8 with a couple much harder. The crags add trad, sport and a little top-roping, mostly 5.7 to 5.12 with a few harder lines. Yellowjacket Crags hold the most climbs, with the Slablands and Cavern Cliff among them. Yellowjacket Boulder is a single tall, highly featured block standing in old-growth pines, and The Hive is a cluster of medium-sized boulders with good landings.

nm_pena_blanca.blurb: Pena Blanca sits at the southern foot of the Organ Mountains in New Mexico, east of Interstate 10 between Las Cruces and El Paso. A low, colorful outcrop of yellow rock breaks out of the range here, and bouldering dominates, with scores of established problems. Most are easy to moderate, V0 to V3, with a thinner tail up to about V7, so beginners can find plenty to learn on. A handful of short trad lines, some top-rope problems and a few sport routes fill out the rest. South Central holds the most climbs, followed by The Garden, The Volcano and East End.

or_yy_basalt_rimrock.blurb: (yy) Basalt Rimrock is a cluster of basalt walls at Smith Rock in Central Oregon, set on the canyon rim above the Lower Gorge. Trad makes up the largest share, with plenty of sport, a few top-rope lines, some mixed climbs and a handful of boulder problems. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, with most routes at 5.10 and 5.11. The area sees a lot of top-rope use by classes, though there are some good leads. Northern Point and Student Wall hold the most climbs, with Hidden Wall smaller. At Northern Point the walls are short by Smith standards, with cracks and bolted routes, and they sit in shade for much of the afternoon, especially on the left side.
